This patch is just duplicating the logs between the various hosts;  That would generally be incorrect in Redfish, and we should be looking up which host each log entry belongs to.  Unclear how to proceed with this.
I have excluded the EventLog entirely from the tree on multi-host for now.

> That would generally be incorrect in Redfish

Can you kindly help me to understand this one? Had a look into the redfish data model spec and found this one:

> The LogService schema contains properties for monitoring and configuring a log service. When the Id property
contains DeviceLog , the log contains device-resident log entries that follow the physical device when moved from
system-to-system, and not a replication or subset of a system event log

When looking at a response from bmcweb, the ```Id``` property is ```EventLog``` so i assume that it is fine for the response to be a replication of a system event log?

If there is currently no way to filter event log entries for the host they belong to, what is the more useful behavior? Having no logs or a duplicate?

Sorry for the late reply, just saw this.

EventLog is something OpenBMC specific, that is not the problem.  Redfish relies on a CRUD model, so if you expose two instances of EventLog on two different hosts, it technically means EACH host had those events.  That's not correct in the way redfish is modeled, and would lead to duplicates on any consumer.

> If there is currently no way to filter event log entries for the host they belong to, what is the more useful behavior? Having no logs or a duplicate?

Having duplicates is for sure incorrect.  Having no logs is allowed in the spec.  Which is more useful is debatable for the clients, ideally we'd just follow the spec here.


FWIW, the whole issue is that EventLog probably needs to be moved to Manager, for which there is only a single instance, but I get not wanting to take on that refactor.

### practical problems and further consequences of requiring unique Log Entries per-bmc

In case a of a 4-blade server, the common 12V drops below a threshold, generating an EventLog entry. Do we now duplicate that entry 4 times just so it has it's own unique id? 

Imagine blade 3 is missing. So now the code generating (dbus-sensors) or aggregating (bmcweb/rsyslogd/phosphor-logging) sensor events has to know which blades are plugged to duplicate the event the correct number of times?

Mind that we also would need to do this in an atomic way such there is no point in time where anyone can query only one of these Log Entries, they must all be added to the LogService in one step.

Oh, and they must also fill the ```RelatedLogEntries``` property since these duplicates all refer to the same underlying event.

And if you want to *Resolve* or *Delete* the EventLog entry, do that 4 times also?

### redfish client must already handle duplicate EventId

> That's not correct in the way redfish is modeled, and would lead to duplicates on any consumer.

Redfish clients already need to deal with duplicates since different BMCs generate their ```LogEntryId``` for the log entries independently.

So currently they already have to handle this case and assume Event Log entries to be unique only in the context of a single ComputerSystem.

> Having no logs is allowed in the spec. Which is more useful is debatable for the clients, ideally we'd just follow the spec here.

That's definitely not useful.  That means we can't manage a multi-host system.

> FWIW, the whole issue is that EventLog probably needs to be moved to Manager, for which there is only a single instance, but I get not wanting to take on that refactor.

I think this is reasonable but it potentially breaks backwards compatibility.  Is this ok?

Alternatively, I think we have a few cases we need better support on overall (and I'm writing this because maybe it helps point us at a solution):
     - "no host"
     - "single host"
     - "multi host"
     
Right now a lot of the URIs are only working for "single host" and in that model there is this view that "chassis" == "host" and so much of the URIs are ambiguous along those lines.  For "no host", like Ventura, I think there are a good handful of URIs that are exposed but aren't appropriate; in that case we end up with an internal server error, due to missing object mapper lookups, rather than a clear "this URI doesn't exist".  On "multi-host", well we're working through all of that here.

I suspect there is some benefit in a split between the "chassis" (being the whole box, mostly managed by the BMC) and the "host".  For single host maybe we continue to represent that as the "Systems/system" URI.  For no-host and multi-host maybe there is benefit in splitting the two such that: "Systems/system" (or "Systems/chassis") represents the "chassis" and "Systems/systemN" (or "Systems/hostN") represent the "host".  In this way it might make it clearer how to turn on or off the URIs appropriately.

> > Having no logs is allowed in the spec. Which is more useful is debatable for the clients, ideally we'd just follow the spec here.
>

> > FWIW, the whole issue is that EventLog probably needs to be moved to Manager, for which there is only a single instance, but I get not wanting to take on that refactor.

It would need to be a meson option to not break existing code.  Too many things hardcode the existing path, and for single host systems.

Lots of code wasn't the best when it came to mapper lookups and handling "0 instances" of an interface".  I see oliver is already fixing some of them, if there's more, please send patchsets.  In what we document, 0 interfaces present should not be an error, and any 500 error that can actually be seen is a bug.  It's just not an easy thing to audit unless you start removing interfaces.

For no-host and multi-host maybe there is benefit in splitting the two such that: "Systems/system" (or "Systems/chassis") represents the "chassis" and "Systems/systemN" (or "Systems/hostN") represent the "host".  In this way it might make it clearer how to turn on or off the URIs appropriately.

Honestly, how to model multi-host in Redfish is getting to the edge of my Redfish knowledge.  We're probably at the point of engaging DMTF with appropriate questions about what gets logged where.

FWIW, this was one of the things that was solved by the suggestion that HOST0 have all the normal "assume one host" interfaces, and Host1-N have only the interfaces that we've ported to multi-host.  Your logs would be on Host0 until they're moved or ported, and the redfish tree would be immediately useful on one node.  I get you guys had your reasons for not doing that, but just giving options.

> FWIW, this was one of the things that was solved by the suggestion that HOST0 have all the normal "assume one host" interfaces, and Host1-N have only the interfaces that we've ported to multi-host.

I am wondering how we would model this in redfish. Would this virtual HOST0 be part of the systems collection and we explicitly disable all other routes on HOST0 that can be handled by HOST1-N? or does it silently exist? I am mostly concerned about validation.  

> FWIW, the whole issue is that EventLog probably needs to be moved to Manager, for which there is only a single instance, but I get not wanting to take on that refactor.

This feels like a straight forward solution.

Let's add a meson option for keeping it on "System", which people can disable if they don't need the backwards compatibility, but also add it to the BMC everywhere (no matter the option).  Is this ok?

> Would this virtual HOST0 be part of the systems collection and we explicitly disable all other routes on HOST0 that can be handled by HOST1-N?

My thinking originally was that host0 would be the "real" host0, not virtual at all, but if you wanted to do that, that would get you guys enabled too.

We have a meson option already for some of this.  https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/meson.options#L177

At this point, I suspect we just need a multi-host option that will live a long time.  That's unfortunate, but given how stuck we seem to be, and how I don't see many others going with this architecture, I don't see another option.  Said option would move some of the logging entries location to the not-per-system location until we have a way to split out per host logs from per bmc logs.

single-host is "host0"
multi-host is "host1 - hostN"

I think this is why Oliver asked about a "virtual HOST0" because there shouldn't be one on multi-host.
Fair enough.  Then host1 would contain all the "default" interfaces.  Or you could add them to host1 to simplify.  Up to you guys.
